title: Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: even if some ministers grew sluggish, the doctrine is not thereby false — abuse of Paul's teaching and of divine foresight (Augustine's monk) does not silence truth
pass_a_gloss: I answer, although thence some ministers would be rendered sluggish, yet it is not effected that the doctrine in itself is false or evil. From the doctrine of Paul some caught occasion of license, saying, Let us do evil that good may come. From the doctrine of Divine foresight, there was a certain Monk (Augustine relating it) who, when the brethren corrected him as he did certain things not to be done, and did not do things to be done, answered again and again, Of whatever sort I now am, such shall I one day be as God foresaw me about to be. That Monk both spoke truth, and by this truth did not profit unto good, but unto evil. For such little objections therefore those things which are truly said of predestination and reprobation are neither to be denied, nor to be kept silent.
pass_b_english: I answer: even if some ministers grew sluggish from it, that does not make the doctrine itself false or evil. From Paul's teaching some took occasion for license, saying, Let us do evil that good may come. From the doctrine of divine foresight, Augustine tells of a monk who, when the brethren corrected him for doing what he should not and leaving undone what he should, answered again and again: Whatever I am now, I shall one day be what God foresaw I would be. That monk spoke truth — and used that truth not for good but for evil. For such little objections, then, what is truly said of predestination and reprobation is neither to be denied nor kept silent.
source_text: Respondeo, etsi inde ministri nonnulli segnes redderentur, non tamen efficitur doctrinam in se falsam aut malam esse. Ex Pauli doctrina nonnulli captabant occasionem licentiae, dicentes, Faciamus mala ut veniant bona. Ex doctrina praescientiae Divinae, fuit quidam Monachus (referente Augustino) qui corripientibus fratribus cum quaedam non facienda faceret, et facienda non faceret, identidem respondebat, Qualiscunque nunc sim, talis olim ero qualem me Deus futurum esse praescivit. Ille Monachus et verum dicebat, et hoc vero non proficiebat in bonum, sed in malum. Propter hujusmodi igitur objectiunculas ea quae de praedestinatione ac reprobatione vera dicuntur, nec neganda sunt, nec tacenda.
